conbody.p: Paimon Impala adds experimental support for Apache Paimon tables registered in the Hive Metastore. You can create and drop those tables, and query the latest snapshot. Impala supports the Hive catalog and the Hadoop catalog.
For more information on Paimon, see .
Impala can do the following with a Paimon table:

ul.li: Create a managed table, or register an existing table with CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE, using the Hive catalog or the Hadoop catalog.
Define partitions, a primary key, and fixed buckets when creating a table.
Query the latest snapshot with SELECT, including primary-key tables. The Paimon reader returns the merged rows and applies deletion vectors that are already part of the snapshot.
Show the schema, the files in the table, and statistics that are already stored with the table.
Drop a managed table, which also deletes its data files, or drop an external table from the Hive Metastore without deleting its files.

conbody.p: Impala reads tables through the Paimon reader. It does not write rows, change the schema, or select an older snapshot. See Limitations for the statements Impala rejects.

When you have an existing Paimon table that is not yet present in the Hive Metastore, you can use the CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE command in Impala to add the table to the Hive Metastore. Impala supports the Hadoop catalog and the Hive catalog. If the table is already in the Hive catalog and you use the same Hive Metastore, you need no further actions.

ul.li:
HadoopCatalog. A table in the Hadoop catalog is stored under a catalog location in the file system. Set paimon.catalog to hadoop and set paimon.catalog_location. An external table also requires paimon.table_identifier.
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE paimon_hadoop_cat STORED AS PAIMON TBLPROPERTIES('paimon.catalog'='hadoop', 'paimon.catalog_location'='/path/to/paimon_hadoop_catalog', 'paimon.table_identifier'='paimondb.paimontable');

p.codeblock: CREATE [EXTERNAL] TABLE [IF NOT EXISTS] [db_name.]table_name ( [col_name data_type ,...] [PRIMARY KEY (col1, col2)] ) [PARTITIONED BY (col_name data_type [COMMENT 'col_comment'], ...)] STORED AS PAIMON [LOCATION 'hdfs_path'] [TBLPROPERTIES ( 'primary-key'='col1,col2', 'file.format'='parquet', 'bucket'='2', 'bucket-key'='col3' )]

conbody.p: Create rules:

ul.li: PRIMARY KEY (col1, col2) and the primary-key table property are equivalent. Do not specify both. Every name must be a column of the table.
Declare partitions with PARTITIONED BY. The partition table property is rejected.
Fixed buckets use the bucket and bucket-key table properties. Every bucket-key name must be a column of the table. CLUSTERED BY is rejected.
file.format is parquet or orc. When the property is omitted, Impala does not set it and Paimon uses its default file format.
Unless deletion-vectors.enabled or full-compaction.delta-commits is already set, Impala sets deletion-vectors.enabled to true.
Other table properties are stored as Paimon schema options. SHOW CREATE TABLE hides storage_handler, primary-key, and partition, and prints the primary key as a PRIMARY KEY clause.
A managed table must list its columns. Impala does not infer the schema of a managed table. Creating a managed table fails when the location already contains a Paimon schema.

An external table may omit the column list. Impala then reads the schema from the existing Paimon table. If the statement lists columns and a Paimon schema is found, that schema replaces the columns in the statement. If no schema is found and columns are listed, Impala creates a new Paimon table at the location.
Setting external.table.purge to true is rejected for both managed and external tables. A Paimon table cannot be cached in HDFS.

li.b: Partitioned table with a primary key:
External table with no column definitions:
li.p: For an external table, you can omit the column definitions. Impala infers the schema from the underlying Paimon table. For an external Hive-catalog table, LOCATION is required. A Hadoop catalog table uses paimon.catalog_location and paimon.table_identifier instead of LOCATION.

conbody.p:
Use DROP TABLE to remove a Paimon table:
DROP TABLE test_create_managed_bucket_paimon_table;

DROP TABLE on a managed Paimon table removes the Hive Metastore entry and deletes the data files in the table directory. DROP TABLE on an external Paimon table removes only the Hive Metastore entry. DROP TABLE ... PURGE also deletes the data files of an external table. If an external table already has external.table.purge set to true in the Hive Metastore, DROP TABLE deletes the data files as well. Impala rejects that property when it creates the table.
SELECT reads the latest snapshot. Impala does not accept FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF or FOR SYSTEM_VERSION AS OF on a Paimon table.

For a primary-key table, the scan returns one merged row per key. It does not return the raw changelog. Deletion vectors that belong to the snapshot are applied by the Paimon reader. Impala projects the scalar columns referenced by the query.

WHERE, joins, ORDER BY, LIMIT, and COUNT(*) are evaluated by Impala. Predicates, including predicates on partition columns, are applied after the scan. Impala does not push predicates into the Paimon reader and does not prune partitions while planning the scan.

An existing table that has ARRAY, MAP, or STRUCT columns still loads, and its other columns can be queried. Reading a complex column fails. Since EXPAND_COMPLEX_TYPES defaults to true, so SELECT * expands those columns and fails too. List the scalar columns, or run SET EXPAND_COMPLEX_TYPES=false as a workaround to query the table without expanding the complex columns. CREATE TABLE rejects these column types. Virtual columns such as INPUT__FILE__NAME are not available.
DESCRIBE and SHOW CREATE TABLE show the schema Impala loaded from the Paimon table. SHOW CREATE TABLE prints a primary key as a PRIMARY KEY clause.
SHOW FILES lists the data files and deletion files in the latest snapshot, including each file's path, size, partition, and erasure-coding policy. SHOW FILES ... PARTITION(...) is not accepted.

SHOW TABLE STATS, SHOW COLUMN STATS, and SHOW PARTITIONS display statistics already stored with the Paimon table. Impala does not compute new statistics. COMPUTE STATS and DROP STATS are rejected. SHOW PARTITIONS requires a partitioned table. Column statistics for DECIMAL, DATE, and TIMESTAMP columns are not imported.

concept.title: Supported Data Types for Paimon Columns

conbody.p:
You can get information about the Paimon data types in
the Paimon spec. Impala can create and query the primitive types in the table below. CREATE TABLE rejects every other type.

The Paimon data types map to the following SQL types in Impala:
Paimon type SQL type in Impala
BOOLEAN BOOLEAN
TINYINT TINYINT
SMALLINT SMALLINT
INT INT
BIGINT BIGINT
FLOAT FLOAT
DOUBLE DOUBLE
STRING STRING
DECIMAL(P,S) DECIMAL(P,S)
TIMESTAMP TIMESTAMP
TIMESTAMP_LTZ TIMESTAMP
CHAR(N) CHAR(N), or STRING when N is greater than 255
VARCHAR(N) VARCHAR(N), or STRING when N is greater than 65535
BINARY BINARY
VARBINARY BINARY
DATE DATE
TIME Not supported
MULTISET Not supported
ARRAY Not supported
MAP Not supported
ROW Not supported

CREATE TABLE writes an Impala TIMESTAMP column as a Paimon TIMESTAMP without a time zone. That value is read as stored, in UTC, with no conversion to the query time zone. An existing TIMESTAMP_LTZ column, which is a timestamp with local time zone, is converted to the query's local time zone. Both are returned as an Impala TIMESTAMP. ARRAY, MAP, and ROW columns cannot be created. An existing table that already has them can be loaded, as described under Querying Paimon tables.
Impala rejects the following statements on a Paimon table:

ul.li: INSERT and INSERT OVERWRITE
UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE
TRUNCATE TABLE and LOAD DATA
CREATE TABLE AS SELECT and CREATE TABLE LIKE
ALTER TABLE, including ALTER TABLE RENAME
COMPUTE STATS and DROP STATS
FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF, FOR SYSTEM_VERSION AS OF, and DESCRIBE HISTORY

conbody.p: Impala also does not provide predicate pushdown, partition pruning, HDFS caching, or a JDBC or REST catalog for Paimon tables.
